examined.definitionExcerpt: # Kleio ## Architectural content - **Role/responsibility:** **Harmonia's authoritative Audit Information Management component.** Kleio owns authoritative Audit Capture, creation/management of authoritative audit information, canonical FHIR **AuditEvent** representation, preservation/retrieval of audit history, semantically significant user/system audit activity and provision/preparation of historical audit context for operational and assurance use. [U07](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u07), [AX-08](../../motivation/principle/21d6864657964ba5b03e3f6b5eb29cd5.md). - **Audit Capture:** clients report semantically significant auditable occurrences and necessary context through a **Kleio-provided contract/library/API**. **Clients SHALL NOT be required to construct FHIR AuditEvent resources.** Kleio constructs and manages the authoritative representation; client API and mapping details remain unresolved. - **Information:** FHIR AuditEvent is the authoritative audit-event representation, without requiring every internal Kleio structure to be an AuditEvent. Indexes, correlation structures and prepared historical context may support management. **Authoritative audit evidence SHALL remain distinguishable from derived, correlated, contextualised or prepared historical views.** Existing meaningful provenance responsibilities remain; AuditEvent does not redefine all evidence. - **User activity:** semantically significant access/view, governed search, create/change/delete, submit/approve/reject, disclosure/export, operational action and relevant denied activity may require capture. These are examples, not a universal event taxonomy; “delete” grants no physical managed-information DELETE. Generic UI telemetry/clickstream is outside Kleio; UI security assurance and governance remain **Somebody Else's Problem (SEP)**. - **Collaboration/exclusions:** **Audit is not Governance. Audit is not Assurance.** Kleio may consume Journey information and Dokimasia outputs and provide historical audit context back to Dokimasia, without evaluating assurance or governing the subject. Dokimasia's governed record/result remains authoritative evidence of its assurance activity; its [terminal rules](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#dokimasia-terminal-boundaries) prohibit a separate own-execution AuditEvent and recursive assurance. Consumption of its outputs does not circumvent those rules. #### Mandatory capture authority and the audited Identity > **Subject of audit evidence ≠ authority performing audit capture.** Kleio performs mandatory authoritative audit capture under **intrinsic platform authority** associated with its established architectural audit responsibility. The originating/acting Identity remains evidence recorded by Kleio; it is not the authority under which the mandatory AuditEvent is persisted. Kleio does not borrow that Identity's PEP-Criteria merely to record its activity, including activity denied to that Identity. Identity-derived authority granted to human/system Identities remains resolved and enforced through Themis. Kleio capture executes within established security context and remains governed by Harmonia security policy, with Themis retaining policy evaluation ownership. Mandatory capture is neither a security bypass nor a policy exception. [AX-07](../../../../docs/markdown/governance/architectural-axioms.md#kleio-mandatory-capture-authority) incorporates this adjudication. Where authoritative audit capture is required for a governed operation and Kleio cannot exercise that platform authority sufficiently to capture the required evidence, the governed operation **SHALL fail closed**. Durable target availability remains necessary; authority alone establishes no successful capture. This authority applies specifically to Kleio mandatory authoritative audit capture. It grants no equivalent authority to other components or other Kleio activities. Any proposed equivalent responsibility requires separate architecture adjudication; representation, policy/enforcement mechanics and transaction coordination remain [CDG-43](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#kleio-detailed-contracts). #### Immutable history and longitudinal evidence Authoritative AuditEvents are immutable. An existing AuditEvent SHALL NOT be corrected, amended, overwritten or silently replaced. Correction or qualification SHALL create a **new AuditEvent**, preserve the earlier event unchanged and refer back to it as appropriate. The earlier assertion remains part of historical record. Journey is the governed representation of observed Harmonia activity/progression; AuditEvent is the authoritative audit representation of a significant auditable occurrence. Journey is an important audit source, **not the audit boundary**. A Journey may relate to many AuditEvents; an AuditEvent may exist without Journey. **Journey participation SHALL NOT be a prerequisite for Audit Capture.** > **Reference by default; replicate only where necessary to preserve longitudinal > audit evidence.** Kleio SHALL NOT duplicate authoritative source information merely because it is audit-relevant. Where historical state can be reliably resolved longitudinally, Kleio references it with sufficient **identity, version, provenance and temporal detail**. Version identity alone is not assumed to supply all temporal detail. Only where the authoritative source cannot guarantee retrieval of the information as it existed at the audited point in time may Kleio clone/replicate the necessary source information within or in association with the authoritative AuditEvent to preserve required longitudinal evidence. Detailed FHIR attachment/reference mechanisms remain unresolved. #### Auditability and R1.x/R2.x availability > **Harmonia SHALL NOT perform an auditable activity unless the required audit > information can be authoritatively and durably captured.** > > **If Kleio cannot authoritatively capture required audit information, Harmonia > is DOWN.** Audit Capture is not best-effort and SHALL NOT be assumed reconstructable later from logs, Journey information or incidental operational state. Transaction, retry/failover and health/readiness mechanisms are deliberately unresolved. Kleio retains audit application ownership; Mneme provides governed Context/Pragma access and Mnemosyne **Harmonia Operations & Assurance** establishes durable audit state. For R1.x/R2.x, multiple **independent authoritative audit persistence targets** through Mneme/Mnemosyne are permitted. At least **one configured target capable of durably establishing the required audit information** is sufficient for continued Harmonia operation. If none can establish it, Harmonia is unavailable and fails closed. Target count, selection and whether one/some/all receive an event are unresolved; targets SHALL NOT be called replicas without established replication semantics. > **For R1.x/R2.x, audit data harmonisation between independent Mnemosyne audit > persistence targets is outside Harmonia scope — Somebody Else's Problem (SEP).** R1.x/R2.x guarantees neither identical histories, complete copies of all AuditEvents, automatic convergence, reconciliation after disconnection nor unified cross-target longitudinal history. Different targets may expose different histories; an immutable AuditEvent remains authoritative without its target holding the whole corpus. No future harmonisation/convergence mechanism is selected. - **Standing:** U07 resolves responsibility, representation, immutability, longitudinal evidence, availability and release scope; [CDG-43](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#kleio-detailed-contracts) retains detailed capture/query/correlation/retention/processing and persistence mechanisms. Historical FHIR/operational storage structures remain provenance, without competing with the established O&A semantic alignment.

# Establish Assurance Context

## Architectural content

•
Canonical Name: Establish Assurance Context.

•
Definition: Establishes the governed subject, applicable assurance purpose and criteria, relevant temporal context, and contextual association of sufficient trustworthy source information as evidence required for an assurance activity.

•
Scope: Includes the evidence-assembly responsibility previously described as Assurance Evidence Assembly; no separate evidence-assembly Function is established. Sufficiency is required for conclusion, not assumed merely because context is established; unavailable or insufficient evidence remains explicit.

•
Information Boundary: Source information remains owned by its responsible source Capability. Its use as evidence does not transfer ownership or originating authority. Governed Assurance owns the contextual association that particular information constitutes evidence for a particular assurance purpose. Evidence association and applicable criteria may each be temporal and version-specific; association distinguishes the information state relevant to assurance from its current state.

•
Realisation Boundary: Uses generic EC-02 context-management capability together with EC-14 assurance-specific semantics as documented in §4.1 (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#41-context-management-contribution). Establishment of Assurance Context prescribes no copying, persistence, aggregation, caching or other technical mechanism.

---

## History

### Function Overview — predecessor explanation

Context establishment makes particular source-owned information evidence for a particular assurance purpose, with applicable subject, criteria and time identified. It includes evidence assembly without assuming sufficiency or prescribing copying and storage. This contextual evidentiary association is the assurance responsibility; ownership of the source material remains unchanged.
